title: Most solid Bluetooth connection you’ll find
text:
I originally never thought I’d own these.. I have several Apple products and try to buy other brands just so I don’t come across an an Apple fanatic (I'm actually somewhat critical of them).. I also always want to know if the grass is greener, I want to own the best gadgets regardless of who makes them :) I own Bose Soundsport free and a couple pairs of Zolo liberty plus. I also have used an Anker set with the wire between the buds.
The AirPods, while I have experienced bugs over the years.. they are the most robust Bluetooth connection I’ve used. They literally NEVER cut out when using under normal conditions. I bought the first generation ones because I like that they are small and white, fits perfectly under a hair net that I have to wear in clean rooms for work. Can listen to my tunes and most people won’t even notice I’m wearing em. I have put dozens of yards of space between me and my phone, several tall metal machines that one would think should interfere with the connection. It amazes me how solid they are.
Now, I won’t use these for working out as I sweat quite a bit and I’m certain they’ll fall right out. I think the Bose ones are the most secure for working out.
Battery life is pretty good when they are new. After a year or two you will notice that it declines (based on my experience with the gen1 version). The battery case could definitely have more juice. When compared to the amount of charges you can get with the Zolo’s, puts the AirPods and the Bose to shame.
People like to complain about the sound quality and sometimes about the lack of noise cancellation. But I find that they sound really good, granted I’m not really a sound snob.. easy to please.. IMO neither the Bose or the Zolo sound any better.

text:
They sound great, are easy to charge and store, the batteries last a very long time, and the noise canceling feature works very well. They are really easy to connect to any device too. But they have a tendency to fall out of my ear, and that costs them a star. Maybe it is just my particular ears, but almost every time I use them, one manages to fall out and hit the ground at some point. Because of that, I have to be careful where I use them. Motorcycle rides and river activities are out of the question. Once one fell out while I was on the riding mower, and it took me about ten very stressful minutes to find it. I have since learned that it helps to wrap a bandanna around my head and ears when mowing. Unfortunately this isn't a perfect solution either, as the other day one still managed to fall out and hit the ground when mowing. Fortunately I found it right away that time.

Thank goodness they certainly do seem to be very durable. My kid's Airpod Pros got washed and dried, and they still worked! I heard them clanking around in the drier for 30 minutes, but thought it was just a nickel or something.

Anyway, for around the house or office they are great. But don't think you can trust them to go anywhere.

title: Better Than I Expected!
text:
I wasn't sure how much I would use or like the AirPods Gen 2 when I first purchased but have really been pleasantly surprised by how often I reach for these over my old trusty wired ear buds.

Fit: I had no issues with fit; the Apple EarBuds always fit comfortably and snugly and these were no different. I would say though that if the EarBuds didn't fit then the AirPods probably won't fit either. I've seen some custom accessories to make more snug but imagine they wouldn't sit right in the charging case.

Connectivity: Apple has really made the bluetooth connection seamless which was always a tedious process on other wireless ear buds I've used. I just pop them in my ear and within seconds I hear the chirp that they're connected - huge plus.

Sound Quality: I would say the sound quality is better than good but not quite excellent. I think there is room for improvement in that regard. No interference or anything but the base isn't very deep.

Battery Life: Again, I would say this is any area where it is better than good but not quite excellent. On a full charge the case and buds will get me through about a day and a half before recharging but that is with relatively light usage. It is convenient that they are recharged with a lightning port as I have them everywhere now (work, car, office).

Overall, I would say I'm very happy with my purchase of the AiPods Gen 2.

title: Prefer to Beats Powerbeats Pro primarily for running
text:
I wanted wireless headphones mostly for running, but also to use casually for conference calls and listening to music/podcasts. From the outset I assumed the Powerbeats would be the best for me and got those. While they are very good, it didn't blow me away. It wasn't so much better than the $30 bluetooth headphones I got 3 years ago. I also struggled to get a good fit in my one ear. What made me send it back though, was that it is just too bulky. The carrying case is huge and even the earphones without the case are big, and I didn't just want to put them in my denim pockets, as they have protrusions that might get damaged or break off. Bottom line, you can't just keep them in your pockets "just in case". Every time you want to take it somewhere you have to make space for it somewhere.

So I got the Airpods. I was very skeptical that:
1. They would fall out when running
2. They would not survive the sweat I generate in the Atlanta summer during 13 miles jogs

I watched some YouTube videos testing their water tolerance and I was surprised that people reported them fully functional after a wash/dry cycle (obviously not recommended). I pulled the trigger and bought it and am happy to report that they work perfectly for running. The sounds is good (not quite as great as the Powerbeats), and they don't fall out at all while running. I thought I'd might need an after market silicone casing or ear hook, but found I didn't need it.

The main reason I removed 1 star is because they are very slippery. Even when the Airpods and your hands are dry, it's slippery and prone to falling when taking it out. When the Airpods and your hands are both wet and slippery, they become like a wet piece of soap, almost impossible to handle. Apple should make it a bit more grippy.

Overall, great product and what really sealed the deal is the portability and the fact that I can carry the Airpods on me all the time.

title: Love these!
text:
I waited a long, long time before buying “Apple” ear pods. I have used Skull Candy, Soundpeats, and a host of others. They all have their little quirks and variations. The Apple ones do as well, but not nearly as many. Overall, the quality of these is awesome. The sound is great, it allows for pass through sound so I can listen to music and still hear what’s going on around me, and the charge lasts for several hours.

The downside(s). First, my ears don’t necessarily fit these (or the wired ones that always came with the iPhones), so I have to adjust and push these in every once in a while. I know that’s why they came out with the pro ones with the plastic ear bud. Those will be the next pair I get. Secondly, live listen works great, with one caveat. I would have imagined that the mic used would have been the mics on the ear buds themselves. Nope. It uses your phone mic. So, if you put your phone in your pocket and have live listen on, you hear the phone shuffling around in your pocket. In other words, you have to leave your phone out (laying on your desk, holding it in your hand, etc.) in order to use it with any success. Maybe that changes on other models, but for these, it makes the live listen almost pointless. I want to be hands free, with my phone in my pocket, but be able to hear someone if they talk to me. Not sure what else the concept would have been used for in using the phone mic.

Other than those issues, I really have no complaints. The case charges the pods quickly and multiple times, so you can continue to use them for a long time. Again, sound quality is as good, if not better, than any other ear buds I’ve used. You can set what the functions are, so tapping the right ear twice can mean whatever you want versus tapping the left ear twice.

I am really pleased with these and would recommend them.

title: Left Airpod Didn't Work
text:
This is one of the purchases where everything that could go wrong did go wrong...
The first time I purchased the Airpods with the additional AppleCare, I waited anxiously for them to arrive. I happened to be at home on the expected day of delivery so I was surprised when I saw the delivery status 'Customer Refused Delivery.' Nope. That definitely didn't happen. I called into Amazon's customer service, who told me, "Disregard that status message. They are Airpods - they probably got stolen. Things can go missing between the warehouse and delivery." Uh, ok. They refunded both the Airpods and the AppleCare, as (THIS IS IMPORTANT) the AppleCare, though sold separately, is connected to the device via the serial number when purchased.
Cut to my second attempt at purchasing the Airpods and the AppleCare... I received the Airpods, and like so many others who have purchased them and left reviews, the left Airpod was defective. I returned the Airpods and received a refund with no issue. However, when I inquired with customer service about refunding the AppleCare (because as I mentioned, when purchased, it is associated with the Airpods via serial number), I was told that a one time exception had already been made for me and they couldn't refund it again. So, because of what was an issue on Amazon's end initially, I'm now screwed out $29 for the AppleCare purchase when I was sent defective Airpods.
If you are willing to buy these Airpods after so many reviewers, including myself, provide feedback stating this product is defective, don't waste your money on the AppleCare.

title: Good middle-of-the-road option
text:

Connecting them to my Apple devices (watch, iPhone, iPad) was very easy, and almost instant. I have not tried connecting them to Android phones or Windows computers, so I’m not sure how well they work for those devices.

For an audio device that doesn’t cancel sound, the sound quality is amazing. They are probably a little better than the stock iPhone wired earbuds, for reference. Nothing crazy, but I’m pleased with them. Since they don’t cancel sound, I can also wear them around the house or out on walks with my dog without the fear that someone will try to get my attention and I won’t hear them.

As someone who almost never buys warranties, I would highly recommend the 2-year AppleCare+ subscription for these AirPods, since it covers everything from damage, to theft, to loss.

title: I just don't understand the hype
text:
I finally made the switch to Airpods from my 2016 Jabra Elite 65t and it most certainly been a downgrade. Here are my reasons for feeling so:

1. Battery life is atrocious. With daily use I would charge my Jabra's once a week. They had excellent battery life and the charge case was great with keeping them ready to go. With my Airpods I have to charge daily. Full being fully charged I took them on an hour bike ride and maybe used sporadically throughout the day and by night I had the warning of only having 5% battery, after being in the case.

2. Sound quality is mediocre. The Jabra's fit in-ear and had an element of noise cancellation. The Airpods sit in your ear but have no noise cancellation. Aside from that, the my old Jabra's had far superior sound. There's not much else to say, they're just better than the Airpods here.

3. Price. I paid $150 for the 2nd gen Airpods at Best Buy. I think they're down to $128 now on Amazon. The newer model of Jabra Elite (the 75t) is currently $129 on Jabra's website. Airpods are severely overpriced for what you get and I have the feeling if you looped in other competitors (Bose, Sony, Sennheiser, Klipsch) you would find similar results.

Overall the one Pro I'll give the Airpods is connectivity. I own an iPhone, iPod, and iMac and the Airpods connect very quickly to Apple products. I have been an Apple user since the early 2000s so they've gotten their money out of me from brand loyalty but their quality has really dropped in recent years. I think the only reason they continue to get glowing reviews is based on this loyalty to them. I would strongly encourage anyone looking at these Airpods to check out some of the competitors first. You will find vastly superior earbuds for the same or lower price. But on the other hand you won't be one of the cool kids with white buds hanging off your earlobes.

title: Range Sucks
text:
Let me start this review by saying that I'm using these pods with a Blackberry Priv that has an Android OS, so take that FWIW. Maybe they aren't compatible, or optimally compatible, or whatever since they're an Apple device. I don't know, but the point of having them is to be able to listen to my phone without wires, and they don't allow that very well.

The range is limited, like less than a few feet, and depending on where I'm using them it's less than that. For example, I can be at the gym on an incline bench, set my phone on the floor next to me, and the podcast that I'm listening to cuts out. Maybe there's interference from the gym's piped in music - they work well enough when they're about 10 inches away from me in the rack on the elliptical machine.

This afternoon I was washing my car in my garage. When I was washing the tires I left the phone on the hood of the car, and when I went to wash the rear tires, my podcast cut out. I ended up turning them off them and using the speaker in the phone.

The only time these pods really work is when I'm driving and I have my phone on my lap. YMMV depending on how, when, and where you use them.

text:
I want to like these. They're easy to use, sound decent for music, and they work well for phone calls. But Apple's "one size fits all" scheme doesn't work for me. I should have guessed these wouldn't fit me properly. Apple's wired earpods that come with every iPhone tend to fall out of my ears easily. Why would the wireless version of the same thing be different?

Apple really should offer these in more than one size.

On battery life, I was on the phone listening to music and/or the news at a reasonable volume for about an hour, then I was on the phone for about two more hours. Indicated battery charge went down from 100% to only 25%. Granted, it's a brand new device, so the batteries might not be quite "broken in" yet, but I don't find that impressive.

I'd give these a more of a chance and a longer review, but since they simply don't fit right, they don't work for me. They're going back.

title: A year later and still loving my AirPods
text:
I've had my AirPods for over a year now, and I have to say, I'm still impressed with their quality and performance. I've used them for everything from phone calls and video chats to working out and listening to music, and they've never let me down.

Pros:

Effortless setup: Connecting the AirPods to my iPhone was a breeze. All I had to do was open the case near my phone and it automatically prompted me to connect.
Great sound quality: The sound is crisp and clear, and I never have any trouble hearing my calls or music.
Good battery life: I can wear them all day without needing to charge them.
Good charging case: The case is small and easy to carry around, and it charges the AirPods quickly.

Cons:

Price: At this price the AirPods are not cheap, but I think they're worth the investment for their quality and convenience. I also have a set of cheap wireless headphones that work great, so only spend the money if you have it.

I also bought a cute pink case for my AirPods and it's perfect. It keeps my AirPods safe and secure, and it makes it easy to spot them in my bag.

Overall, I'm very happy with my AirPods and I would definitely recommend them to anyone looking for a high-quality, convenient pair of wireless earbuds.

They seem to stay in my ear well, the sound is crisp and clear and the bass is even decent. I wanted an option to have earbuds that didn’t totally block out the outside world that way people won’t yell at me at home and I won’t hear them.

This type of earbud that is ‘not isolating’ actually is easier to use for dictation and phone calls. The ones that seal tight in your ears are muddy and have skull resonance that makes it hard to make phone calls.

I am not sure of the long-term durability yet, and I am really considering buying the AppleCare protection just in case this new pair has problems. I am upping the review to five stars.

Original review: only two stars.

Now that the price has come down, I decided to try a set of these 2nd gen. airpods. I got an authentic, new pair, they have nice finish and feel, and the pairing details shows I can buy the Applecare extended warranty, so I don't believe they are fake.

I followed the setup instructions, but it only paired one earbud. The other was staticky and then had no audio. When I took out one earpod and put the other in, waited couple seconds, that one has audio. Then when put the second one in, there is only stereo audio for perhaps 5-8 seconds, then one ear gets staticky or drops signal, then just one earpod.

I spent the next 30 or 45 minutes (or maybe an HOUR) 'forgetting' the earpods, resetting the case, re-pairing them, it has the same problems. I have multiple other bluetooth earbuds, headphones, etc., and have not had problems like this. I followed the instructions from Apple to the letter, and searched other websites for ideas.

They just will not play both earbuds at the same time. The signal also loses connection and has signal interruptions, static, loss.

When they do play together, the sound is very good to me, clear, with some bass, and they fit in my ears well. I wanted to try a pair of these so that I can hear ambient noise around me and people, other kinds I have seal tight and you can't hear anything around you (and also phone calls are harder to make since you can't hear your own voice as well.)

I am going to order another set and see if that one will work properly. For $110, and the $30 extra, these Airpods should work perfectly and without all these issues.

I have, for instance, 4 other sets of Taotronics earbuds and they work flawlessly and easily, and they were only $40 each. The Apple earbuds are triple that cost and can't do a basic pairing to my iPhone 13.

If the second set doesn't work correctly, I'll just pass and go with a different company.

text:
I love being able to throw these things in my pocket. I felt they looked a little goofy at first, but I got over that. They don't advertise these ones as noise cancelling, but I swear they do cancel out some of the outside noise, and I don't think that's just in my head, either. They aren't cheap, but I have a pair of these and a pair of Beats Studio Earphones, and that way I can go either way, which usually means I use the AirPods for walks, or going out, and the Earphones are for the beach, or at home (is it just me or is it just a little scary being basically deaf to the world around you at times?)

I think they ought to include these with the purchase of the expensive phones that Apple sells, but that's just me.

One last thing-supposedly the newer generation are more sweat resistant than these ones, but I haven't had any issues there, so I'm not sure what that's all about. It's not like I'm a marathon runner, but I have worn these in the summer on long walks, and besides cleaning them with a q-tip here and there, there's no issues.

The battery life is about 2 hours, maybe a hair less than that, but if you just bring the case with you, you put them back in there and about 15-20 minutes later they're charged again. The case itself needs to be charged every so often, which roughly translates to every 2-3 days, or every 3 charges. They last a long time if they're just sitting in the drawer, not on the charger, which makes them available to use pretty much at all times. As the corny cliche goes, I don't leave home without them.

title: Love Hate Relationship
text:
I'm fully in the Apple Ecosystem: iPhone, iPad, Mac. It was time to replace my wireless headphones and heard so much about the Airpods and so many friends love them, decided to stay Apple. Indeed Airpods work great with Apple products. If that's all you're going to use them for, don't hesitate. I've bought and returned 3 other airbud products. Primary issue was the device staying in the ear, then sound quality. Airpods stay in your ears and the sound is very good for the price point.

HOWEVER........I'm primarily interested in wireless help with hearing especially my TVs. I do not have Apple TV. One TV is a smart Samsung with Bluetooth and the other is Panasonic that I've added a Bluetooth transmitter. Anything that's not Apple has no issue pairing with the TVs. When it comes to pairing the Airpods, my blood pressure rises each time. Sometimes they pair, sometimes not. But that's not the real issue. The Airpods do not have independent sound control. If you're using an Apple device, you control the sound through the device like phone, watch etc. However, my TVs (two major brands) do not have volume control for output. Very few TVs do. So if the volume is too high or too low, I need to disconnect from the TV, pair with an Apple device, get the volume where I think I want it, then disconnect, then re-pair with the TV and hope the volume is somewhere near where I like it.

I spoke with Apple about this and their response is buy an Apple TV device. That way the Airpod will pair and sound can be controlled. In my case, I would need to buy 2 Apple TV devices. The low priced airbuds come with volume control, apparently there isn't any technology magic required. Apple is choosing to not include.

I'm still undecided about returning the Airpods. The fit, comfort and sound are well worth the price. The volume annoyance is a reminder each time I use these things that Apple is not the customer focused/design company we think they are. Before I bought the Airpods, I spoke with 3 friends who use and highly recommend. Each one told me I would be able to control the volume with my iPhone or iPad. After talking with Apple, that is not the case.

While on that subject, since my last Apple purchase this is the first time in about 18 months that I've needed to talk with Apple support. What has happened over there? Four calls in two weeks; each time I feel like I'm speaking with someone that is just reading a script and doesn't really understand the issue. The solution to most any issue seems to be, buy something else Apple. As a long time shareholder who's gone through a lot of stock splits, I appreciate the focus on Apple products but come on, there's more solutions to improving an Apple product than buying another Apple product.

But after fishing it out of a clean toilet with clean water and being disinfected—yes, it still worked!) and one falling into a 425* oven—well, no that one did not survive. Before I could decide if I wanted to risk third degree burns by attempting to rescue my precious AirPod, it slid down under the bottom plate of the oven and burst into flames within seconds. So, here I am buying my second set, and for a great price. I am not a snob when it comes to sound quality (I had a $39 cheap knockoff that I was perfectly happy with, and I still use my wired ear buds from time to time) but after my husband bought me my first set of AirPods I realized how superior the sound is. Easy to pair up with Bluetooth devices and I have no problem wearing them for hours at a time. My biggest problem is—you guessed it, they fall out sometimes—at the worst moments!  Hubby’s told me he won’t buy me anymore if I have another “accident”, but we’ll see...

title: Perhaps not the best option for serious runners
text:
I only use them for running but while doing so there's a few features that I like to have by the quick press of the button/ear bud instead of fumbling for my phone: skip forward, skip back, pause/play, adjust volume and a nice bonus that is rarely used is calling up siri. While you can customize each of the ear buds to perform one of these actions, you can only pick two, and volume adjust is not an option which is a huge problem for me while running at times (i.e. going into and out of traffic areas). The sound quality and battery life is excellent as you'd expect for an apply product but w/o these other capabilities I'm considering returning them because they just won't be used that much and I feel as though the lack of controls will make them annoying. It is nice that they pause automatically when you take them out but sometimes I want a quick tap instead. They also aren't super sensitive so sometimes I double tap and it doesn't do the desired function, then I'm tapping again a little harder. I can't figure out if I'm not hitting it hard enough, quick enough, or the wrong spot. When you're running you really don't want to mess with this too much, it needs to be quick and responsive. I realize this is an earlier generation but not sure why they didn't at least incorporate a single tap and double tap option to provide more features.

I was replacing some much cheaper Mifa X17 buds that only lasted about a year before I started having problems and a few months later they might be totally dead for good (at least one of the two buds). But for the price, I could get 3-4 of those for the same price as these, still have pretty good quality sound and all the features I need for running plus it has wireless charging. I mean that's like 3-5 yr of earbuds for the same price with much more features... I'm not sure I can ignore that. Just another option to consider depending on what your intended use is.

Since the charging case is pocket size you can always carry these with you and since the case contains a seperate battery they're always charging in your pocket. Connecting is a breeze, 1. Open flap, 2. Do you wish to connect airpods ? -> Connect 3. Done...

Airpods with or without wireless charging case?
I have a wireless charging pad and a lightning cable next to my bed and rarely used the pad for wireless charging of these, would just stick with the lightning charged case if you don't need a full charge every day. I only need to charge weekly and since you can charge the case without having the airpods in the case I sometimes plonk it in the charger when I'm going to do stuff around the house and want to use the airpods.

Airpods or Airpods Pro ?
I have both kinds and I really like both types, for different scenarios. When using public transport or really need noise cancelling the Pro's shine, however for extended use, > 1 hour, when riding a bike, out for a walk, eating and listening I go for the classic airpods, they're just more comfortable to wear, you barely know they're there....

title: Worst Apple Product There Is
text:
I really want to like them. They're supposed to be effortlessly convenient to pair and use for all your Apple devices while sounding and looking good. But they're not....they're none of that. Let me explain:

Sound - it's ok, really. No seal so you hear all the ambient noise around you which is good and bad depending on the situation. Not much for bass extension, treble is flat but clear. Adequate all things considered. If you've used the old design earpods, these are nearly the same sound profile. On a plus, the microphones are very good.

Features - very little to say here. They're Bluetooth (5.0) so they pair quickly and have long range, when they work (more on that later).

Battery Life - very good, a couple hours at high-ish volume on the pods and half a dozen charges per case charge. More than I need for most situations.

Functionality - 100% atrocious and I've had 3 sets of these (shame on me). The case and charging system is so faulty it leads to numerous other problems with pairing and connecting both AirPods at the same time. The contact points in the case and on the pods where they charge easily loses connection, dirties, and later corrodes. Using them for fitness around any sweat or moisture will speed up their inevitable failure. Once this happens, one pod will refuse to charge or stay connected when put back in the case, draining it's battery or trying to reconnect to different devices when in the case. Even if they didn't suffer constant bugs, the pairing with multiple devices is equally buggy, frequently losing connection or trying to connect to other devices in the house for no apparent reason.

As far as I can tell, AirPods Pro share the same charging design, so I will listen to my own advice and stay far away from these until the design is fixed. I would advise you do the same.

title: Wow
text:
This thing performs well in all of the standard headphone categories like:
- great sound quality
- stays in ears (at least mine - i'm a normal sized guy, 5'10" 190lbs)
- great battery life
- fast charging
- great noise cancelling
- works amazing as a 2-way (i use it for conference calls while walking down busy streets and airports all the time and rarely get people saying that background noise is distracting)

Where this thing blows away all competition is just the magic of how effortlessly it works. Open the case lid and your phone asks you if you want to set up your new AirPods. Once it's set up, pop them in your ear and whatever you were playing on the phone goes to your AirPods. Then pop them out and whatever you were listening to automatically pauses. You get helpful little sounds when the battery starts running down. To charge them, just pop them back into their case (which itself stores probably 4 or 5 full charges for the headphones) and they'll be workable again in about a minute, and fully charged in about 10 minutes. (I haven't actually timed this, that's just anecdotal)

I get that there are much cheaper wireless headphones out there but anyone who has ever used AirPods can tell you these are another level of convenience and quality. Once you use these you'll never go back to non-Apple products, at least not for use with an iPhone.

title: Although they are amazing, I'm now on my 4th pair in 4 years.
text:
1 star because although they are amazing, I'm now on my 4th pair in 4 years.

I bought my airpod 2nd gen directly from Apple (not on Amazon). My first pair had the microphones go out, but I didn't realize it until just after the 12 month warranty expired. I just thought Siri sucked and couldn't figure out what I was asking. Had I realized it was a microphone issue in time, I would have been under warranty. However, when I finally realized the microphones fully quit working, they wouldn't replace them (days past warranty). Soon after this the speakers on one side started going out. I had to adjust the iphone sound settings to have less sound go to one ear so they balanced out and then up the volume. At this point I decided I'd get a new pair because I use them all the time and need sound and microphones working.

So, I bought a second pair. Fast forward several months and the microphones quit working on this pair. This time I call for warranty asap. They checked things over with me and replaced them. To apple's credit, it was single day shipping and quick turnaround.

So, onto my third pair. About 3-4 months in with my third pair, the microphones quit working. WTH. I am so careful with these things and have no clue how or why this could possibly be happening. I was so busy working at the time I waited to contact support (thought the new pair would have typical 1 year functional warranty expectations). Well I was wrong there. Spent a long time with Apple support and learned that the replacements are only covered for the remainder of your original pairs warranty (or 90 days if your previous pair were under that time remaining). So, they only guarantee the replacements will function properly for the time remaining on your previous product warranty? I get that they don't want people seeking a brand new product every year through minor warranty claims, but what if the replacement product legit fails in a short period of time?

After being escalated to senior support staff at Apple and some more discussions, they ultimately agreed to make an exception and provide me a warranty replacement pair. Sent them in and they confirmed the issue and replaced quickly. Again, quick turnaround with warranty shipping.

So, onto my fourth pair. Everything works great, but it's only been a few days.

I love the airpods. They sound great. I prefer earbuds that don't "plug" my ear and these fit my ears well. Only real issues have been those mentioned above. Another issue has been battery life. It's great when they are newer. Normally, they notify you when they are running low several times before powering off. As they get older, I'll get that low battery sound and then they immediately shut down.

The airpods have amazing reviews and ratings by thousands, so I'm shocked I can't find anyone else having issues with microphones like I am. They are great when they work, but I've had tough luck getting them to work correctly for more than a year.

UPDATE on 4th pair... less than 3 months into the 4th pair and people were occasionally having trouble hearing me in conversations. I isolated the left vs right mic in the settings and figured out the the right airpod microphone is going out (distant soft sound and cutting in and out). Didn't notice earlier because the left still works fine and it must autoselect that mic most of the time. Called apple and looks like I'm still in the 90 day warranty on replaced items (thankfully I caught it in time), so it looks like I may be able to get the right one replaced. Will have to again send the entire case and both airpods into their service center first to have them checked.

I put these in my ears. I put them back in the case. I really don't understand how each pair could keep having this issue.

title: Keeps Connecting
text:
I've always wanted AirPods but found the cost too expensive. I was really happy when I found these AirPods for cheaper and I found the double tap feature really convenient when I'm on the go. Unfortunately, I've experienced multiple issues with them.

I often find the notification that my AirPods are connected when they're in the case and the case is closed. I thought it was because I was using an older phone, but I just got the new iPhone 13 and the issues persist. It's pretty annoying to have the notification because while it's at the top of my screen, I can't swipe down to access the notification bar, and it takes a while to go away. There was a time when I was playing music through the speaker and the music stopped because my phone said my AirPods had connected.

I've also had issues with the double tap feature. There are times when my music pauses by itself and though my hair sometimes brushes against, I just don't think it can mimic a double tap. There are also times when the headphones won't respond to a double tap.

Lastly, they die so quickly! I don't know if this is normal for all AirPods but it feels like I'm constantly having to charge them, whereas my other Bluetooth headphones can run for days on a single charge. I'm pretty bummed that these didn't work out.

title: ***LOUD*** calendar alerts may damage hearing and no way to adjust volume
text:
The loudness of calendar alerts is a deal-breaker. It is maximum volume and seriously likely to damage your hearing and/or give you a heart attack. When the alert goes off you claw at your skull to rip these out of your ears it is that bad. I have thrown them across the room.

This is a known bug with these.

I researched this for days and the best i found was one method to adjust volume (kill all apps, reduce volume, use as normal( but as soon as you adjust the volume through a different app or on another set of Bluetooth speakers, it goes back to maximum.

There is no practical way to control this.

If you use your Airpods and phone for business and have a lot of calendar alerts, the Airpods suck.

On the positive side, the sound is pretty good.

They also charge very rapidly in the case - very pleasantly surprised at that. I get about 4 - 5 charges from the case's battery before that has to be recharged.

The feature for checking the battery on your iPhone by opening the case near the phone is also very cool.

If they could fix the calendar bug they would be 5/5 rated.

text:
I have both the AirPods and the Jabra Elite Actives. I like them both but for different reasons
AirPods Pros
- light,
-comfortable,
-Wonderful phone call performance (at both ends)
- great charging case
-5 hour battery life
- open design allows you to hear traffic, conversations, etc (this is a negative in noisy environments)
AirPod Cons:
- will not stay in without earhooks
- Not water/sweat proof.
Jabra Pros:
- great sound isolation (especially with Comfort tips)
- better base than AirPods,
- good battery life,
-not as obtrusive as the q-tip AirPods
-Much better water/sweat protection
Jabra Cons:
- the absolute worst customer service you will EVER find. Hope you will never have to use it. I had to return two before I got a pair that worked. THANK YOU AMAZON!

If I had to buy just one, it would be the AirPods. But, the Jabras are better in the gym or in noisy environments.

text:
(Honest review: I paid full retail price and received nothing of value for this review.)

I liked these a lot--until I tried the AirPod Pros.

Sound quality is more than adequate, not the best, and convenience with iOS devices is great. I primarily bought these for use working on videoconferencing and telephone calls. They worked very well.

For these purposes, however, get the Pro version. In addition to being more comfortable* and less prone to falling out than the AirPods, the sound is at least as good and the noise cancellation is awesome! It makes all the difference for working. After trying the Pro version, I gave away my AirPods.

*Usually I find "intrusive" ear buds uncomfortable and expected that the AirPods would be more comfortable for me than the Pros. This is not what I found. The Pros are the most comfortable "intrusive" ear buds I have ever tried (including many premium manufacturers' offerings).

It's like someone gutted a real pair of airpods, replaced the internals with cheap knockoffs and put it back together. EVERYTHING with my "airpods" was identical and seemed brand new. Plastic wrap was around the oem box (pretty easy to fake nowadays, but still impressive nontheless). Everything was immaculate just like a new box of airpods, OEM feeling cable, etc. The feel, touch, glue, placement of holes and patterns of the airpods seemed identical to my older airpods.

1. The biggest clue was audio quality. The audio quality was considerably worse than regular airpods. It was noticeable right off the bat, especially when talking with other people. It was especially obvious since I still have my old gen 2 airpods to compare with.

2. Bluetooth was very unstable. Leaving more then 6 feet away from my bluetooth adapter made it go haywire and produced a lot of static. It would also randomly go offsync with the left and right earbuds when listening with both of them on.

3. Battery life. They lasted about 2-3 hours before the battery died on them. Not much else to say about this, just way lower battery life than new airpods should have.

Interesting thing to note, the Apple limited warranty should NOT be used as a metric to see if it's legit. The first thing I checked was to see if these fake airpods had warranty, which it said I had 1 year starting from the day I paired it with my iphone 9/22/22. I thought this assured me that I had a legit pair of airpods. Once I concluded the new airpods were fake, I did some testing and all I did was put my real old airpods with the new fake airpod charging case, and now my old airpods purchased in 2019 said I have 1 year of warranty starting on 9/22/22.

CONCLUSION: BUYER BEWARE, HIGH EFFORT AIRPODS SEEM TO PLAGUE AMAZON. If you want to save ~$25 bucks and roll the dice get these on Amazon. If you don't want to take the risk of dealing with this headache, just buy it directly off Apple.

Connects instantly! You can’t change the volume on it without pulling out your device unfortunately. In my opinion it’s a tad over priced. If you want them I personally wouldn’t pay more than $70. Only reason I got them was because I had gift cards that covered most of the cost so I really only paid like $40 Or so for them. Overall is it worth money not really definitely cheaper options that are probably the same quality in all honestly. If you are heart set on Apple products these are the best option. This is the OG one but personally I would get these over the new ones less to go wrong. Again only if you heart set on Apple if not get the like 30-50 dollar ones will be just about the same quality and features as these. Also buy the case with something to attach to like a purse, backpack or, pants definitely something you can lose if you travel a lot! They do appear in find my iPhone app but if they haven’t been used it will just show the last location. So someone would have to use them to keep the location up to date. Again you have to decide if this product works for you and is worth your money personally if you don’t care if it’s Apple get the cheaper one if you can’t buy non Apple these are the best ones that you can get without spending a crazy amount of money! Side note don’t buy them used! Used ones usually have issues that Apple won’t cover unless you buy Apple care so unless you want to buy Apple care on used ones just buy them new!

If you have an Android and want Airpods, buy them. You won't get all the features iPhone's get but it's totally worth it.

text:
I have an iPhone and wanted a good pair of wireless headphones but without Apple's price. After trying about 6 different brands and returning them or just wasting money on them I decided to bite the bullet and just get the Air Pods, now I wish I did it sooner. They sound great, I like that I can just say Hey Siri to change the volume, and they are so useful. I use them daily when working by either listening to music when working on a project or talking to customers, I also use them when mowing the lawn or just running to the store. These do not noise canceling but they isolate the background noise well but not to the point where you cant hear around you. I am surprised on how long the battery actually lasts for such a small package, also the storage case/charger is great because if I am running low on power I just plug them in for 15 min or so and have enough power to take several more calls.

I would recommend these to others and I am even going to buy a pair for my fiance to replace her off the wall wireless earbuds.

title: Gen1 vs Gen2
text:
A lot of people are asking if these are Generation 2. Here's what I found.

The box itself reads "Model A2032 A2031 A1602". ... verbatim on the packaging... if you want to look up the details yourself.

The package includes A2032 and A2031 left and right AirPods. Apple calls both 2nd generation. And the package also includes a A1602 case. Apple calls this Lightning Charging Case with no specific mention of generation.

From what I can see, Apple never quite calls the included Lightning Charging Case a gen 1 product but lots of other sellers do. Some of the confusion is born here.

Year of introduction tells a story too. The Lightning Charger Case (this one) debuted alongside the Gen1 AirPods in 2017. The Wireless Charging Case (the one some people are expecting) debuted alongside the Gen2 AirPods in 2019. Yet Apple is pairing the newer AirPods with the older charging case.

So no amount of confusion here! :) I'd call the case that comes with this a gen1 myself.

A lot of reviewers are crying foul. But the product is not mislabeled from what I can see. The Apple store sells the same product as "2nd Generation."

Kind of a bummer. I bought specifically for wireless charging. Didn't expect all this confusion. Returning both.

title: The most overrated earbuds on Earth
text:
Decided to see what the hype was all about and bought Airpods. While they are admittedly aesthetically pleasing and pair nicely with Apple products, I just don't see what the hype is about. They're incredibly uncomfortable and fall out of my ears whenever I walk or laugh (and yes, I have tried orienting them differently in my ears to no avail). If they're not falling out, they feel incredibly loose and like they are about to fall out. I looked online to see if other people were experiencing this and how to fix it, and found some articles about how airpod covers are available to allow the earbuds to stay in place. For the price I'm paying for these earbuds, why do I need to buy another $13-20 product to make the $135 product actually possible to wear? Absolutely ridiculous. Why should anyone have to exert additional effort to actually make the product functional? After messing around with the Airpods, I finally gave up and put on my ($10 ) earbuds that have the same sound quality and infinite more comfort than Airpods. I really do believe that Apple is the only company on this planet that can get away with its product being designed so poorly that methods to make their product wearable have to be created.
I also noticed that switching the Airpods from my Macbook Air to my iPhone XR was a hassle. I would have to tap the option to forget my Airpods on my iPhone and then reconnect them after using them with my Macbook Air.
Finally, I know people who swear by these earbuds. They work well with other Apple products and look good on the wearer, but I don't think that these reasons justify the price tag or all the other cons I've listed above.

title: Almost seamless integration
text:
I'm cheap. This was in large part why I resisted shelling out the money for these. Consequently, I tried several other Bluetooth earbuds, several on the decidedly cheap end of the scale. One of the problems I experience is finding earbuds that fit my ears. I have very small ear canals, so the earbuds that have the cone shape tip that fits into the ear canal either just won't fit, or are extremely painful after a short time. The only shape I've found that actually works for me are these, which I discovered with the first pair of wired Apple earbuds that came with a new iPhone several versions back.
I included this picture, which shows the Airpods on the left and the much cheaper knock-off I tried. I thought I'd be okay with the shape of the cheap ones, but as you can see, they are actually much larger than the Airpods, so they were frequently falling out of my ears, especially when I was doing any physical activity.
So, I bit the bullet and shelled out for the OGs. Here's my take:
Pros:
-Integration with other Apple products. I have an iPhone, iPad and Apple watch and these work quite seamlessly unlike any others I've tried. I put "almost" in the title because I'm sure it will be improved on in further versions, I'm just not sure how. Oh, and I've never used "Hey Siri" as much as I do with these. I love being able to adjust the volume (among other commands) hands free. True story: Yesterday I was riding a scooter home from work, and not wanting to remove either hand from the handlebars, I wanted to use Siri to increase the volume. There was enough ambient downtown noise that Siri was having trouble hearing me, so as I was tootling down the busy city street I was saying "Hey Siri" repeatedly at increasing volume, until I was shouting it. Not one of my finer moments...
-The fit (see above)
-Quick charging. I will have something to say about the battery life in Cons, but one saving grace is that they charge remarkably fast. I do a lot of work from my computer (like a lot of others during the time of COVID), so I appreciate being able to get a quick charge on them between meetings.
-Sound quality. I am not an audiophile, so my opinion here is very pedestrian, but they seem to have a good dynamic range. I've been blown away by the bass response coming out of such a small thing.
Cons:
-They still are not very secure in my ears. I suppose that could be more my issue than the Airpods, but I did have to buy an aftermarket accessory kit that included the silicone tips with wings and a silicone lanyard. Sometimes I commute to work on an electric scooter, and if it weren't for those (particularly the lanyard) I would have dropped one of them in the street multiple times. Sometimes I walk over a grate in the street and have a brief moment of fear that one will pop out of my ear and through the grate. With my luck, it isn't so much an issue of "if", but "when". (Side Note: if Apple doesn't sell replacements individually, they should)
-Battery life. I figure I get about 2 hours of active use, which is fine and I think what they advertise. The curious thing is that the two discharge at very different rates. I'm trying to keep track so I can take them into our local Apple store and ask about it, but it is odd, and I have seen other reviews that also noted that issue.
Overall, I give them 2 thumbs up!

I think you can only make an outgoing call using Siri. I dont like or trust siri, so i will have no choice but to use manual phone functions to make call, answer call and disconnect call. Tapping will forward or go back to previous songs, pause, play, siri connect, (annoying as siri dont always do what you ask). So i dont use siri for that reason mostly. Volume is only controlled manually on device, or again, by using siri. By the time i get siri to do what i want, its faster using regular functions. title: They're OK. I wish I bought them elsewhere though.
text:
I was hesitant to purchase Airpods because of the steep price so when I saw there was a deal a few months ago (early 2020) I hopped on the bandwagon! Since I have many Apple products, these DO make it easier to sync up to my Macbook, iPhone and iPad. However, even with that being the case the airpods I received were defective. I spent hours talking to customer service and at the Apple Store (pre-COVID) and they ended up having to replace the case and one of the airpods. At times I still have issues with connectivity and the microphone isn't the greatest. Sometimes my airpods would be in the case and I wasn't trying to connect to my phone yet the music would play WHILE THEY WERE IN THE CASE. I even reported this to the apple care team and my customer service representative told me it was something they'd never seen or heard about before. (Seriously wish I was making this up, I just wanted to be able to have wireless earbuds).

I'll admit that I don't fully regret my purchase, but regret buying it via Amazon instead of from the Apple Store or a major retailer (i.e. Best Buy). Not sure if my logic makes sense, but I feel like there would've have been less of a chance of getting a faulty item.

TLR; Airpods aren't a bad investment, but be wary and monitor your item if you buy it via Amazon. ALSO they aren't noise cancelling and the microphone isn't the greatest. The sound is OK but if you want to still spend a good amount of money, you probably can get better quality headphones elsewhere. The best feature to me is that it is super connected with my apple products and I can tap to change the songs, etc.

title: Great for Calls and casual Listening; Tough for a Hardcore Workout
text:
The title of this review kind of says it all--these AirPods are amazing for everyday things like phone calls, listening to music while travelling, and other low-impact activities. The sound is really great, linking them to my iPhone was super easy, and the battery life is really good. If you're looking to ditch the corded headphones and you're someone on the go, this is a fantastic purchase.

All that said, I originally bought them because I was looking to hit the gym pretty darn hard to get rid of some of my Covid padding. When I work out, I get really sweaty (ya girl is working HARD), so I find that halfway through my workout, they don't always stay in my ears very well. I make it work, but there are some points where the ear piece feels like it's going to come flying out of my ear if I don't stop and adjust.

I'm still going to give these 5 stars because they are pretty awesome, and I use them for so many other thinks outside of working out, but if you're looking for some AirPods to use while working out and you're a sweaty Betty, I'd look to get ones that are built with a bit more of a sports mode.

I have to say that I just got these AirPods and I LOVE them! Just to state my bias upfront: I love Apple products, but I’m not an Apple fanboy. Lols

PROS: The sound quality is fantastic. I have owned Bose and Jam ultra earbuds. These are on par with the Bode product. Though I have never owned the first generation of the AirPods. I like how easy it is to pair these with my iPhone. It was so quick and simple. The Bose and Jam were cumbersome at times, often I would have to unpair and repair them to get them working again. No such thing with the AirPods. I love the small container that stores and charges them. It just looks and feel nice in your hand too. The Bose were big and clunky and the Jam Ultra case was huge and made a bulge in my pocket.

CONS: My negatives for the AirPods are small and very trivial. I wish that they were a little more snug in my ear. The Bose and Jam earbuds did fit more snugly in my ear hole. Also with the AirPods it doesn’t give me a battery level status at the top of my phone screen. See my uploaded picture. The Bose and Jam Ultra both had a battery level status bar next to the headphone icon at the top of my phone screen. With the AirPods I have to get the case and open it to get a status of the battery level. Very insignificant, but it is something.

I love these AirPods and am extremely happy with them! I highly recommend these earbuds!

title: Too many issues for the price
text:
Overall, sound is fine. They’re just earbuds so I don’t expect audiophile levels of sound quality or any noise cancellation. But for an apple product, these things have far too many bugs for their price.

These things are terrible outdoors or in very large spaces. They will cutout and disconnect, because I’m assuming the signal is too weak and doesn’t have anything to bounce off of. That makes them basically useless for the outdoors or in wide open spaces, like large atriums or gyms. I can really only expect to use these in the home or office, which meant I had to buy another pair of headphones that worked outdoors. It’s a bit ridiculous.

Speaking of home and office use, the mic does not work well at all, and is unusable for phone calls, video/zoom calls, etc. So again, I have to switch to a headset or my other pair of headphones for that, since people cannot hear me if I attempt to use these.

On top of that, they also have issues with ear detection and randomly disconnecting from my iPhone. I’ll be wearing them, listening to whatever, and suddenly they just drop the connection, as if I took them out of my ear. The only way to get it working again is to place it back into the case and take them out again and place them back in your ear. It’s very annoying and happens almost every time I use them.

I’ve used two pairs since 2018, and both have had these issues. I’ve only used them with other apple products, multiple iPhones and an iPad, so I know it’s not a device compatibility or Bluetooth issue.

My oldest pair has almost no battery life left, and is only useable for less than an hour at a time, so don’t expect these things to last more than a few years either.

In conclusion, these have always felt like a step backward from a classic pair of wired earbuds. Sure, they’re wireless, but it just feels so much less usable in so many different ways, while being 10 times the cost. Apple needs to seriously step up their wireless earbuds game if they insist on moving away from wired connections and forcing us to use the garbage pods.

title: Compared to 1st Generation
text:
This is the 2nd generation airpods 

List of changes: 

1.  H1 chip (vs W1 chip) supporting hands-free "Hey Siri". 

No need to double tap on earbuds, just use voice controls. It's like a portable Amazon Echo, Google Home smart, Apple home pods device on your ears (but only for Apple devices).

May feel a bit odd talking to your airpods in public, but as it catches on, people will just shrug it off especially in a city setting

2. Better battery life. 

Up to 1 hour more talk time depending on volume setting and distance away from phone, apple device

You get around 4 hours talk time and approximately 6 hour music playback per full charge

3. Faster device connection times. 

Not by much, maybe half a millisecond. 

Answer calls 2x faster than original (less lag when picking up calls)

===

Misc info/features:

Audio remains the same as first generation. Sound quality very similar stock wired Apple earbuds. Audio very smooth, no lag or audio hiccups 

Has two microphones. Audio quality from recipient are similar to wired counterparts. Apple claim it helps filters out background noise, but does not work as well as other noise cancelling headsets. I personally can't tell difference from wired ear pods. Unlike wired, you don't have to lift/hold up mic to your mouth when other party can't hear you which is a plus.

Fit. Varies by person due to ear shape. Slightly tighter/snug fit than wired counterpart. If those don't fall off on their own (without tension/tug on wires) when out-and-about and doing physical activities then these won't either. 

Built-in accelerometers and optical sensors. Able to pause audio by tapping on earbuds or double tap for Siri. Again able to use voice controls by saying "Hey Siri" without tapping. Detects in-ear placement, which enables automatic pausing when one ear bud is taken out of the ears. Can resume with one ear piece on ear, but need to hit resume on Apple device.

Compatibility. Works with any device that supports Bluetooth 4.0. Also works with Android, but won't have the seamless auto switching between devices via icloud/Apple ID. When using Android it acts like regular bluetooth headset. For the price, it's not worth it on Android unless you like the visual aesthetic, as there's better options out there. For Apple users with multiple Apple devices it very convenient; just set it up once via bluetooth/sync button on case, and don't worry about audio syncing across Apple devices. This feature is compatible with devices running iOS 12.2 or later, macOS 10.14.4 or later, or watchOS 5.2 or later.

Optional wireless charging case can be purchased separately and is also compatible with 1st generation AirPods. Wirelessly charge via any Qi wireless charging pad, takes 1.5 longer for full charge compared to wired charging.

This version charges via lighting cable. Takes around 3 hours for full charge.Very easy to drop wireless earbuds in case for storage or charging. Has a very satisfying click sound when closing lid.

Airpods and charging case has own separate battery indicators viewable via Apple device. 

Case holds 4-5 charges for airpods when full. 

Has a find phone feature and vice versa. Airpods will make a sound at max volume and give approximate GPS location on app. 

No water resistance, no soft touch texture like on Apple pencil (feels like wired Apple earpods with cords cut out and longer/thicker stem).

Conclusion 

Overall, wireless version of the stock wired Apple earbuds you get with your iphone with better features. Seamless audio pairing across all Apple devices with Apple ID registered, very convenient and life changing after you use it for a while.

 

Not recommended for Andriod users unless you like how Apple Airpods looks. 

If you own first generation, not worth the upgrade unless you plan to use the hands free "Hey Siri" function often. 

Another option you can get is the Power Beats Pro which also have H1 chip and similar features. title: Excellent convenience, sound quality, battery and design make airpods worth the price!
text:
Love these!
Bought multiple sets for the entire family! The sound quality of the 2nd generation airpods has certainly improved from the 1st generation. The sound is still crisp, but the "bass" is greatly enhanced. This brings the new generation nearly up to the five-star level of earbuds like the $300 Stennheiser Momentum True Wireless 2.

Apple's airpods aren't built for complete noise cancellation. Although the ear-form shape of Apple's airpods help prohibit background noise somewhat, if you're looking for complete noise cancellation you'd be better served looking for earbuds designed for that purpose, like the $228 Sony WF-1000XM3. However, if you're like me and don't mind simply upping the volume a notch or two, Apple airpods will do just fine.

The contoured shape has another benefit: the airpods stay in very well while doing activites. I took them for a run with no issues, and played a little basketball and only had to readjust them a couple times.

The battery life of Apple's airpods is as good as advertised, giving close to five hours of music playback in my test. Unless you're going for multiple marathons per day, they will more than suffice.

The hallmark of airpods are their convenience. They automatically pair with your phone as soon as you open your case. The case, by the way, is as smooth and chic as it looks. The pods are touch controllable, meaning you can skip, rewind change volume, and control calls all with a tap. The call quality is great as well, almost better than an actual phone.

In summary, for the fine-tuned product that Apple airpods are, the price is a bargain!

text:
I have always hate Apple earphones since they used to be inferior sound quality and and not comfortable to wear. However, they changed all these stereotypes when they released Earpuds and then followed Onkyo, they offered TWS airpods. Good sound quality considering its price, CHEAP. Highly competitive product.
As a tech enthuast. I have purcahsed quite a lot of all different earphones, the TWS type. I used to hate all wireless earphone but now they seems improved quite a lot. I have Sony WF-1000XM3, Master Dynamic MW07, countless all different Chinese brands model (One did impressed me but it did not last longer than 3 months and dead) plus 3 pairs of this Apple AirPods. As well as some Senn and Bose products. Thus, I think I am 100% qualified to say something related to a product.
Pro:
1. Very easy to use, swip, double click and you have full control. Very little learning cost. The easist one to use by far.
2. Good sound quality. Apple used high efficiency code to encode and decode bluetooth signal, AAC. It performs just like a pair of wired earphone. I think they can compete with Senn CX300II or so. Great.
3. Tiny case, premium look and just right material used.

Con:
1. You would be very very easy to left it somewhere. As I said, I have purchased 3 times of this exact same product from Amazon. Why? I lost it earlier last year, bought again in Black Friday and left somewhere a while befoe, it did not last more than a month. And now I am getting my latest 3rd pair. What a funny thing to mention. Apple should consider to provide insurance to this product. lol
2. Poor noise cancellation function. I know it is only a passive NC earphone but Senn CX can do far better job than it. It just make no sense why Apple cannot improve it. Particualrly when I am also using a Sony ANC earphone. Hell and heaven difference.
3. Short battery life. neither of the charging case or the earphone itself. They claims 4hours battery life but in real situation, you get up to 3hours which is far from enough. For music enthuast, you should consider to have at least 2 pairs of them, then you can switch when you have to charge.

PLUS, Comparing all my other earphones. I think Apple is more like a good compromise combination, it excelled in some aspects like sound quality, signal but not that good in noise cancellation, or feel of this case(I prefer MW07 case much more than a plain plastic case made by Apple). In a word, I recommend this product.

text: I have problems with the Audio becoming desynced and some annoying issues with old firmware. There was also a rather nasty bug with the model I received. It nearly made me deaf - if you don't know to update the thing (which is a problem for Android...) then you might suffer some hearing damage. I used them for days with the bug and was on the cusp of returning them. The bug is that the audio defaults to maximum volume - with any device (iOS, Android, etc) - until the software is updated. This volume setting reverts to maximum everytime the device enters a power saving state. They sleep aggressive (like maybe 5 seconds of silence). So, if you're streaming music and it takes more than 5 seconds to fetch the next song -- you're getting blasted at full volume force from a device directly inserted into your ear. Very painful. Again, if you just update them they're fine. I was able to reproduce the problem on multiple devices and it wasnt until I updated my airpods that the problem went away. Now the only problem I have is the occasional desync of audio. It's easily fixed and a lot of other people have the same issue sadly. I have noticed that holding the phone differently affects the rate at which desync occurs, so probably just something with signaling. Leaving the phone flat and uncovered/held remedies my issue. When they work, they're really nice. But overall the initial frustrations really took it's toll on my ability to like this product. Hopefully there's better QA on the next generation.

title: Fantastic earbuds, but underwhelming compared to 1st gen
text:
Owned a pair of 1st gen Airpods and they were fantastic; I was blessed with compatible ear canals and all was good. That pair was stolen/misplaced, so I figured I'd just "future proof" and go with gen 2 when replacing them. Got my 2nd gen Airpods and they were also fantastic. If you're looking for a quality pair of BT earbuds that "just work" then I'd absolutely recommend either G1/G2 (assuming a typical wired pair of Apple earbuds fit you well).

However, the changes between generations is incredibly minimal and if you aren't someone who cares/uses the quick charging, it's doubtful you'd notice a difference between the two. Sure a new chip and wireless charging are indeed improvements to specs, but they offer limited actual use-case improvements. I assumed that the battery must've been improved in the 2nd gen models, but it's literally the same exact battery: 398 mAh case battery & 93 milliwatt battery for the actual pods. I'm a longtime Apple user who grew to love their products, but within the last couple years I've branched out and started building PCs as a hobby and it all started, because I just got fed up with what the company has become in the Tim Cook era. It's why I wasn't surprised when I figured out gen2 was essentially a rehash. About a month ago, my late 2008 unibody Macbook (not pro) had finally been retired; after a solid 11 years of service that included upgrades w/ a SSD + 4x stock RAM I decided it was time for a new notebook not because of hardware performance, but actually due to Apple locking those older models out of OS/Safari updates. I took a look at some current model MacBook pros and it's so disappointing to see how far this company has fallen. I became an Apple user because at the time I knew I was getting top quality hardware that would justify the pricetag by providing longevity and overall value thanks to the ease of user-repairs. The hardware is still quality today, but the price premium is no longer justified as rather than paying for the option of future hardware upgrades/longevity, you're now paying a premium just because it's Apple. It's a slap in the face to consumers and a practice I can no longer support. I'll continue supporting innovative products like Airpods where there (wasn't) another market competitor, but I refuse to continue buying Apple because Apple.

Tl;DR: Fantastic earbuds, but don't upgrade if you already have a pair of gen 1 pods.

text: Mixed feelings on this item.  I have a pair that I have had for about a year and a half that still work well.  I only use them a few times a week, but other than the fact that they constantly fall out of my ears, I like them.  If I wasn't able to find the aftermarket silicone ear hooks that I need to use to keep them from falling out all the time, I would have returned them and give them a 1 star rating.  To be fair, I have small ears.  So, I would consider another option if you have small ears.  That said, this review is for a second pair I bought as a gift.  Unfortunately, after 6 months the right pod would not charge/work at all.  The left one would work, but only for about 20 min.  If fully charged and left in the charging case, both the case and the working pod would completely drain, which implies the batteries are not good in the case or the pod(s).  The person I bought these for didn't tell me about the problems until several months after she noticed it.  So, I had her give them to me and contacted Apple.  Support was really good and they tried to help me get them to work over the phone.  Unfortunately, no luck.  So, I asked what my options were to get them replaced or fixed.  They said they were out of warrantee and it would cost over $200 +$12 S&H to get them repaired.  I paid under $150 for them, so naturally all I could say was thanks for the help...  I guess I'll just throw these in the trash.  There are a lot of options out there that are a lot less pricy.  So, I will replace the gift, since I don't like to give a gift that is defective.  However, I may look at the Samsung or a couple of others that are out there.  Again, the ones I own still work fine.  This pair was obviously just a "lemon", but since Apple wasn't willing to do anything, I have a bad taste in my mouth.  Pretty disappointed with Apple. text:
Battery pros:
I generally use only one per day, and it can be out of the case all day!
I recharge the entire thing once a week or once in two weeks and it works throughout.
Battery cons:
No wireless charging.

Sound pros:
The sound is great, the noise cancellation works as well as the pro. Music sounds so real and when talking on the phone the person on the other end always hears you.
Sound cons:
NONE!

Specs pros: It's thin and easily fits into any of your pockets, including shirt, pants, coat etc. I like it more than the pro because it's not as wide as the pro, it's narrow so therefore more versatile.
Specs cons: This is for all Apple airpods in general. Because it's white it's easier to get dirty or get visible scratches. Not sure why, or maybe it's only mine.
Fit: It fits so well into my ear, it doesn't fall out when walking, sitting/laying down or when doing house chores. It sits comfortably in my ear as well.

In conclusion, I definitely recommend this to anyone looking for an easier life! This frees your hands in so many ways, including using Siri, not holding your phone when talking, listening to music or anything else you can think of that involves talking or listening. The size is appealing, the price is definitely good, and battery life a hit.

title: Returned Due To Muffled and Low Volume Microphone
text:
I've been using some cheaper options, but decided to upgrade to the real deal. I've seen people using these in TV interviews and figured they must be the best.

Unfortunately, for my uses, which are mostly recorded video interviews via Zoom, etc., the microphone was awful. Versus a cheapo $30 lav mic, the mic on the buds sounded very muffled. No crispness on the high frequencies at all. Worst of all, people could not hear me on the other end. The output volume for the mic was extremely low versus everything else I've used. I tried adjusting the audio settings in Zoom and other programs, but still no good even at 100% volume.

Maybe it sounds great when used with iPhone or an Apple device (I don't know), but performance when paired with my Windows 10 laptop was too poor for my uses. It paired fine and I could hear fine but the muffled, low-volume microphone was a deal breaker for me.

title: They are just amazing!!!
text:
These are the best pair of wireless earphones I ever came across, apple has definitely done it again. Being an apple fan, I love these! They are so easy to connect! Once I connected them to my iPhone, they were seamlessly connected to my other apple devices. All I have to do is select them in the list from the device you need them to connect and you are good to go. Another good thing is turning them on/off is easy, just remove them from the charging case and they turn on and put them back to turn them off, its simple. And like most of the earphones out there, they connect to the last device you used them with, but its easy to switch device.
You have the flexibility to just use one piece, if you like and sometimes it does come handy. Another function I like is the automatic ear detection, just remove a piece from you ear and playback will pause and resume once you put it back, this does help when someone drops by for a conversation and you don't need to actually pickup your phone to pause the playback.
The battery life is definitely impressive, I need to charge the case every 2 days. And it's easy to carry everywhere, it being so small.
Now the sound quality is crisp and connection is smooth, I found that the 2nd gen AirPods are actually better and improved on 1st gen, but its not worth to upgrade, but if you are planning to get your first one, I would definitely say go for the 2nd gen AirPods, I got a pretty sweet deal on amazon and am very happy with my purchase.

I'll keep them because they sound great, but am a bit disappointed about that one thing.

title: Amazing Sound Quality but Some Cons
text:
Update: I've had these for six months and the case has stopped charging. They are essentially useless now. I would recommend purchasing through Apple so you can get another pair if yours malfunctions. Since I purchased on here and the return window is closed, I cannot get another pair, which means $130 down the drain.

This was definitely one of my best Amazon purchases. The sound quality on these is amazing even during phone calls. The charging case holds an impressive amount of charge so I only need to recharge it once every 2-3 days, which isn't very much considering I use these 8-10 hours a day.at work. That being said, there are some cons to these. The battery life of the AirPods themselves isn't the best-- you'll get 1-2 hours max. Now, five minutes in the charging case will get these back to full charge, so take that with a grain of salt. The biggest con for me has been the Bluetooth connectivity. I have an IPhone 11 so I would expect these to have no issues with connecting. However, every few times I use these, one or both of the AirPods does not connect when I pull it out of the case. It usually takes about five minutes to figure out the problem and re-connect them. It's definitely a problem when I'm trying to pick up a call on my AirPods or listen to something quickly. For that reason, I'd give these 4/5 stars. They're still worth the purchase but I'd recommend adding AppleCare so you can get a replacement if you have the same issues. (P.S. If you have an Apple watch, these do not connect independently to the Apple Watch, you will need to have your IPhone on you.)

title: Some Great Features
text:
Ever since I switched from Android and PC, I've become Apple-centric. Since Apple products like Apple products, I decided to buy some Air Pods. Amazon's Prime Day price of $114 finally brought them down to what I considered a little bit better price, so I bought them.

Pros:
1. They connect very quickly with all my Apple devices.
2. The sound quality is a few steps above some of the other ear buds I've had. The stereo is good, and while they don't have enough bass for me, they don't sound tinny either.
3. They fit fairly comfortably in my ears, although the right pod fits better that the left one does. Maybe I have an oddly-shaped left ear!
4. So far, neither pod has fallen out of my ears. However, I've worn them mainly in the house, so I don't know how it would be if I was running. That, I'll never know because I don't run anywhere.
5. The case opens very easily, and the pods are fairly easy to remove. I really appreciate this because my Jabra case is so hard to open that I would often have to get my husband to do it for me.
6. I love, love, love the fact that I can say "Hey Siri," and get so many things done. I was watching an Amazon Prime show on my iPad Pro the other day, and I told Siri to mute the volume, and she did it! However, when I said to un mute, that didn't happen. Maybe I need to figure out some other terminology for that. When I said to rewind a couple of seconds, it did that, too. This is a really great feature.

Cons:
1. Other than the price, the one thing that kept me from buying these was how silly they look with that long white stem protruding out the ear. One person said they look like a hair dryer, and they do. I have noticed that the Air Pods Pro have a much shorter stem, and thus they look more normal. I guess when the get down low enough in price, I'll probably buy them and give these to a friend or relative.
2. They don't have noise cancellation, which I would really love to have. I guess I'll have to wait for the Pros for that.
3. I didn't realize that they had wired and wireless charging versions, and I ended up with the wired ones. However, I bought a wireless charging case for less than $10 from Amazon Warehouse, so I'm going to see if that works.

Overall, other than some of the cons I mentioned, I really do like these. They connect quickly, have a pretty good sound, and the hands-free Siri feature is great. However, I would say that if you can afford them, you should get the Air Pods Pro because they look better, and they have more features. If you can't, these would be a great stop-gap measure until the Pros go down in price.
